ai_summary: Scotland's clean energy generation continues to outpace local grid export capacity today, creating substantial economic and environmental friction across the British electricity system. Great Britain wind output currently stands at 11.2 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output contributing 4.2 GW, representing 41.6% of installed Scottish wind capacity. While Scotland maintains an exemplary carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh, the GB-wide figure sits at 62 gCO2/kWh due to thermal generation elsewhere on the network. Because of severe grid bottlenecks, 9,696 MWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a constraint cost of about £516,890. Replacing this clean electricity required an estimated 1,842,316 m3 of gas to be burned in other regions, producing 3,394 tonnes of CO2. Annualising today's constraint spend indicates an estimated total yearly curtailment cost of £189 million. Apportioning this system-balancing cost across standard national electricity demand increases everybody's invoice in the UK by an estimated £0.70/MWh, underlining the critical financial and environmental imperatives for accelerating grid transmission reinforcement between Scotland and England.
